title: Sell Mineral Rights in Murrysville, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Murrysville, PA | Westmoreland County
metaDescription: Murrysville, PA is where Pennsylvania's natural gas industry began in 1878. We buy Westmoreland County mineral rights directly, old leases and new alike.
heroLead: Murrysville has a claim almost no other place in Pennsylvania can make: the Haymaker well drilled here in 1878 is generally credited as the state's first commercial natural gas well.
intro: That history matters for mineral owners today because it means some Murrysville-area deeds carry gas leases and reservations going back further than almost anywhere else in the state, layered now under more recent Marcellus development. Sorting out which agreement governs which depth on your specific parcel takes real title work.

We buy mineral and royalty interests around Murrysville directly. Given the town's long gas history, we're used to working through older documents alongside newer Marcellus leases to figure out exactly what you own.

sections.heading: From the Haymaker Well to the Marcellus
paragraphs: Murrysville's shallow gas wells supplied Pittsburgh for decades after that first 1878 well, and some of those old leases, or the reservations tied to them, are still technically on record. The deeper Marcellus formation is a completely different target, and modern operators have leased and drilled it separately across Westmoreland County over the past decade and a half.
If your family's deed references an old gas lease from the early twentieth century or earlier, that doesn't automatically affect your Marcellus rights, but it's worth confirming rather than assuming.

sections.heading: Suburban Growth Over a Historic Gas Field
paragraphs: Murrysville has grown into a Pittsburgh suburb over the decades, and a lot of the old gas-field farmland is now residential. As with other growing areas, that doesn't erase mineral rights that were severed or retained separately from the surface long before development arrived.
We research your chain of title through the Westmoreland County Recorder of Deeds in Greensburg to confirm exactly what you hold, regardless of what's built above it today.

sections.heading: What We'll Walk You Through
paragraphs: Before any offer, we'll explain your division order, any historical lease documents we find, and current royalty performance so you understand the full picture.

faqs.question: Does Murrysville's old gas history affect my current mineral rights?
faqs.answer: It can add research steps to confirm which agreements are still active and at what depth, but historic shallow-well leases typically don't affect deeper Marcellus rights. We verify this for your specific parcel.

faqs.question: My property is now a subdivision. Can I still hold mineral rights under it?
faqs.answer: Yes, if minerals were severed from the surface before development, those rights can remain with your family regardless of current surface use.

faqs.question: Is Murrysville still seeing new Marcellus drilling?
faqs.answer: Operators have continued developing Westmoreland County acreage over the years, and we check current activity specific to your unit as part of our review.
